findings.claim: README line 51 and the implementer report state that a non-JSON or non-documented provider response shape maps to `invalid-response` (spec: "non-JSON or schema mismatch -> invalid-response"; documented shape `{ success, data: { web }, id?, warning?, creditsUsed? }` with only id/warning/creditsUsed optional).
findings.evidence: src/lib/pricingResearch.server.ts lines 96-103: `firecrawlSearchResponseSchema` marks `success` AND `data` as `.optional()` and the whole object `.loose()`, so any JSON object passes. Probe run with an injected fetcher (node --experimental-strip-types --test on a scratchpad file importing the real module): `Response.json({})` -> result with 0 candidates; `Response.json({"error":"quota"})` -> result with 0 candidates; `Response.json({"success":true})` -> result with 0 candidates. The panel then renders "No public supplier links were returned for this query." with a nominal credit estimate, i.e. an untruthful success state for a body that matches nothing in the documented contract. The test "malformed JSON and undocumented shapes are invalid-response failures" (src/lib/pricingResearch.server.test.ts lines 174-183) only covers non-JSON text, `web: "not-an-array"`, a flat `data: []` array and an empty body; the `{ success: true, data: {} }` case at line 122 is asserted as a success, so no test covers an object that lacks `success`/`data` entirely.
findings.fix: Make `success` and `data` required in `firecrawlSearchResponseSchema` (keep `data.web` optional if an empty search must be tolerated, or require `success === true` explicitly), and add server tests asserting `{}`, `{ error: "x" }` and `{ success: true }` (no data) each throw `invalid-response` with zero candidates kept. Then correct the README/report wording to match what is actually tested.
